corrections: glossary.json:first-set:definition: For a grammar symbol sequence, the terminals that can begin strings derived from it, with an empty-string marker when it can derive nothing. LL(1) choices must also consider following tokens when an alternative can be empty. → For a grammar symbol sequence, the terminals that can begin strings derived from it, with an empty-string marker when it can derive the empty string. LL(1) choices must also consider following tokens when an alternative can be empty.

glossary.json:pratt-parsing:definition: Vaughan Pratt's 1973 parsing technique in which each token has a prefix handler and an infix handler with a binding power. It is essentially the same algorithm as precedence climbing. → Vaughan Pratt’s 1973 top-down operator-precedence technique, using token-specific prefix and infix handling with binding powers. Its binary-expression core is closely related to precedence climbing, while the token handlers also organise prefix and other forms.

glossary.json:recursive-descent:definition: A hand-written, top-down parsing method with one function per grammar rule; each function calls the others as the grammar says, so the grammar becomes the code. → A top-down parsing method that implements grammar rules with functions calling one another. Parsers can be hand-written or generated; straightforward predictive versions use token lookahead to choose alternatives.

glossary.json:parser:definition: The compiler stage that checks a list of tokens against the language's grammar and builds a tree recording how they fit together. → A component that recognises input according to a grammar and commonly builds a syntax representation. Calc’s parser consumes tokens; scannerless parsers operate directly on characters.

glossary.json:lexer-hack:definition: The technique C compilers use to tell a typedef name from a variable name: the lexer consults the symbol table, filled by the parser, so `T * x;` can be lexed as a declaration when T is a type. → A technique used in some C parsing architectures to distinguish typedef names from ordinary identifiers: token classification consults symbol information. Other compilers can resolve the distinction in the parser or semantic analysis instead.
glossary.json:lexer-hack:source: https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg14/www/docs/n1570.pdf → https://clang.llvm.org/doxygen/classclang_1_1Parser.html

glossary.json:immediate-operand:definition: A constant encoded directly inside a machine instruction, such as the 8 in `mul r0, r0, #8`, so it needs no register. → A constant encoded directly inside a machine instruction rather than fetched from a register or memory. The accepted values and encodings depend on the instruction set.
glossary.json:immediate-operand:example: None → In AArch64 `add x0, x0, #8`, the immediate operand 8 is encoded in the instruction.

glossary.json:tree-tiling:example: x86's `lea` can cover the whole pattern `a + b*8 + c` as one tile. → x86 LEA can cover a base register plus an index register multiplied by 8 plus a constant displacement of 16 in one instruction.

glossary.json:callee-saved:definition: A register a called function must restore before returning if it uses it, so the caller's values in it survive the call. On x86-64 System V these are rbx, rbp and r12 to r15. → A register a called function must preserve according to the calling convention, saving and restoring it if necessary. The x86-64 System V preserved registers include rbx, rbp, r12 to r15 and the stack pointer rsp.
glossary.json:callee-saved:source: https://llvm.org/docs/CodeGenerator.html → https://gitlab.com/x86-psABIs/x86-64-ABI/-/jobs/artifacts/master/raw/x86-64-ABI/abi.pdf?job=build

glossary.json:coalescing:definition: Giving both sides of a copy `b = a` the same register when they do not interfere, so the copy can be deleted. Conservative coalescing only merges when it cannot make colouring harder. → Assigning both sides of a copy such as b = a the same compatible register so the copy can disappear. Conservative coalescing uses sufficient tests intended to preserve colourability when merging interference-graph nodes.

glossary.json:cil:definition: Common Intermediate Language: the stack-based bytecode that .NET compilers such as C#'s produce and the .NET runtime JIT-compiles. → Common Intermediate Language: the stack-oriented instruction language used by .NET assemblies. A .NET implementation can JIT-compile it, while ahead-of-time compilation is also available.
glossary.json:cil:source: https://llvm.org/docs/CodeGenerator.html → https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/managed-execution-process

glossary.json:tail-calling-interpreter:definition: An interpreter design in which each opcode handler is a small C function that ends by tail-calling the handler for the next opcode. CPython 3.14 offers it as an optional build with Clang 19 or newer. → An interpreter design in which opcode handlers are small C functions that tail-call the next handler. CPython 3.14 offers an optional implementation requiring Clang 19 or newer on supported x86-64 and AArch64 targets.

glossary.json:polynomial-time:definition: A running time bounded by a fixed power of the input size, such as n squared. Problems solvable this way are considered tractable. → A running time bounded by a fixed power of the input size, such as n squared. Polynomial time is a conventional theoretical notion of tractability; a high exponent or large constant can still make an algorithm impractical.

glossary.json:state-explosion:example: Remembering the last 20 characters needs 2^20 = 1,048,576 DFA states. → For the language requiring the twentieth character from the end to be a over alphabet {a,b}, the minimal DFA needs 1,048,576 states.

authorCorrections: AOT can use runtime profiles collected earlier; PGO is not exclusively an AOT-only activity.
Rust regex is a third-party crate, not the Rust standard library; single-search and repeated-search bounds differ.
A C lvalue need not be modifiable; a const-qualified object can still be an lvalue.
Left factoring does not guarantee the entire grammar LL(1); FIRST/empty-alternative analysis also needs following tokens.
Not every AST removes parentheses, and token-based parsing is not the only parsing architecture.
SSA is static single assignment with available definitions, not single execution; LLVM phi placement, loop headers and incoming-edge semantics qualified.
C signed left shift requires a nonnegative left operand, even when a negative multiplication result would fit.
JVM max_stack counts long/double values as two units, unlike the one-value Calc model.
Register-allocation/coalescing and live-interval claims now state interchangeable-register, equal-value, ABI and side-effect assumptions.
W^X does not imply every JIT must use one specific permission-switching technique; runtime deoptimisation destinations and performance costs vary.
Geometric mean does not automatically neutralise outliers; cache misses may hit another cache rather than main memory.
Swift’s parser is no longer incorrectly included in a universal precedence-climbing claim; TypeScript parser evidence is versioned.
The branch label in the SSA drawing now agrees with its C/LLVM example.

gaps: This preserves a teaching compiler made of excerpts, not a packaged standalone Calc distribution. Parser wrappers, complete checker scaffolding, identity/simplify/show helpers and several target emitters are supplied only in scratch to execute the published portions.
Production instruction scheduling, full instruction selection, global register-allocation implementation and real native JIT machine-code emission remain conceptual as in the original scope.
No HotSpot/PyPy/LuaJIT runtime was executed here; their mechanisms are primary-source checked. No Apple iOS JIT entitlement/deployment experiment was performed.
The Sethi–Ullman, interval-allocation and liveness fixtures are finite exact models under the lesson’s explicit register/evaluation assumptions, not arbitrary target-allocation proofs.

x86-64 output was cross-compiled and inspected but was not executed on this AArch64 host. Actual LLVM phi code and AArch64 target examples were executed; iOS entitlements, HotSpot, PyPy and LuaJIT were source checked only.
